archetype.name: Pocket Passer (downfield-leaning)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower who wins from the pocket with anticipation into the middle and over the top, barely runs, and lives or dies on how long his line holds up.

report.headline: The downfield leap is real, but a leaking line is swallowing it whole
report.take:
Through seven starts Young has been two quarterbacks. The first four weeks showed a real step forward. He is averaging 274.4 passing yards a game, fourth in the league, and his yards per attempt is up 0.84 on last season even as his completion rate fell 4.9 points. That trade is intentional. He is throwing into tighter windows (aggressiveness up to 13.38%) and pushing the ball downfield, and those throws pay. His 29 deep attempts are worth +0.833 EPA apiece with an 11-point CPOE, and the intermediate band adds +0.503. Throws between the numbers have been his best work all year: 72.3% completions, +0.627 EPA, no interceptions.

The last three games tell a different story. He has posted -0.199 EPA per dropback, a -9.9 CPOE, a 10.8% sack rate and 13 sacks. The schedule explains much of that. Tampa Bay ranks 2nd in defensive EPA and Green Bay 7th. The Green Bay game came on four days' rest with starting guard Damien Lewis (89% of snaps) ruled out, and his center left that game hurt. You can see the line problems in the throws he chose: his intended air yards fell to 6.8 against Tampa and 4.7 against Green Bay, against 10-plus in most of his good games. He has been pressured on 29.8% of dropbacks, 37th of 38. A 26.4% pressure-to-sack rate is middling, and slightly worse than his 2024-25 form. The sacks are mostly a protection problem he isn't escaping, not a habit he has always had.

The averages also blend a strong downfield game with a broken short one. Throws at or behind the line have cost the offense -21.3 EPA on a -15.1 CPOE. That is mostly screens and swings that aren't blocked or aren't timed, and it drags everything under 10 air yards to roughly zero value. Third down (-0.236 EPA, 10 sacks) is where the pressure hurts most, because long-yardage downs let rushers pin their ears back. The red zone is a mixed bag: 9 touchdowns and no picks, but a 28.9% success rate. The touchdown count is better than the down-to-down play.

The Panthers pass more than situation predicts, second-most in the league, so his volume will stay high. The question is whether his efficiency settles near the first month or the last three weeks. My read is in between, closer to his season line than his recent slump, provided Lewis returns. That holds against average defenses, not against fronts that win quickly.

strengths.title: Deep and intermediate accuracy
strengths.body: His throws of 10-plus air yards carry nearly all of his passing value, with a positive CPOE at both the intermediate and deep levels. This is a real development from a player whose career aDOT ran 6.9 to 8.7. It held up across opponents early in the year. It disappears only when protection forces him to dump it short.

strengths.title: Owns the middle of the field
strengths.body: Between the numbers he completes 72.3% with a +12.1 CPOE and no interceptions. That fits a timing passer reading leverage and working Tetairoa McMillan and the tight ends inside. McMillan has been worth +0.344 EPA a target on a team-high 66 looks. This is skill and scheme, so it should last.

strengths.title: Volume baked into the offense
strengths.body: Carolina's pass rate over expected ranks 2nd. That is why he sits 4th in yards per game and on a 4,665-yard pace despite middling efficiency. As long as Dave Canales keeps calling it this way, his counting stats have a high floor.

concerns.title: Pressure and sacks are piling up
concerns.body: He is among the most-pressured quarterbacks in the league, and his sack rate has climbed to 10.8% over the last three games. The cause is mostly up front: a starting guard out, a center hurt, and two of the league's better defenses. His pressure-to-sack rate was a top-13 mark the last two years, so I expect some correction if the line gets healthy. Behind a patched line it will stay a problem.

concerns.title: The screen game is a dead zone
concerns.body: Throws at or behind the line have lost more EPA than any other area of his game, on a -15.1 CPOE and a 23.8% success rate. Some of that is execution on his end. More of it is blocking and design on plays that need both. The result is that his easy completions don't function as an extension of the run game the way they should.

concerns.title: Third downs bleed drives
concerns.body: He converts just 34.3% of third downs with an average of 8.2 yards to go, and 10 of his sacks have come on third down. Long yardage plus a leaky line is a bad mix. It won't change much until early downs improve and protection firms up.

trend.note: He was efficient in three of the first four games, including +20.5 EPA against Detroit. The last three have run negative, bottoming out at -20.3 in the Tampa Bay blowout. That slide lines up with tougher defenses, a short week and line injuries rather than a sudden loss of skill.

nextGame.headline: Denver takes away his best throw, but its safeties are thin
nextGame.body:
Denver is a bad matchup for how he wins. The Broncos rank 7th against the pass, 4th in deep EPA allowed, and 2nd in QB hit rate. That is a defense that gets home and caps the shots that carry his season. The softer spots are underneath, where they rank 17th in short EPA, and the tight end, where opposing TE1s average +0.46 EPA a target, 30th. That points to a game plan of quick throws inside to Darren Waller and McMillan rather than a vertical shootout. Denver is also soft against the run (26th in rush EPA), so a more balanced Carolina plan would protect him.

Availability could tilt it. Starting safety Talanoa Hufanga (93% of snaps) is out, and fellow starter Brandon Jones (91%) is questionable with a hamstring. Losing both would open the deep middle that Denver's numbers say is closed. On his side, Damien Lewis carries a return date of this game; getting him back is the single biggest swing for his protection. The center spot is uncertain with Corey Bullock questionable. Xavier Legette and Jonathon Brooks may be designated to return from IR, which would add depth rather than change the plan. Ten days of rest after the Thursday game helps. The Book has Carolina as a 3-point home underdog with a 43.5 total.

keyMatchups.title: Panthers line vs Denver's pass rush
keyMatchups.body: Denver's 21.8% hit rate ranks 2nd, against a quarterback already pressured on nearly three in ten dropbacks. If Lewis plays, the protection math improves. If not, expect another game where he is forced short and sacked several times.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots vs a depleted secondary
keyMatchups.body: His deep game is worth +0.833 EPA an attempt, and Denver allows -0.087 on deep throws, 4th-best. Those numbers were built with Hufanga and Jones healthy. With one or both missing, the shots he hit in September become more realistic.

keyMatchups.title: Tight ends over the middle
keyMatchups.body: Denver has been gashed by top tight ends, and the middle of the field is his most efficient area. Waller at +0.345 EPA a target fits the hole the Broncos have shown.

nextGame.watch: Whether Damien Lewis is back at guard. That decides if he can hold the ball long enough to attack Denver's thinned-out safeties, or gets pushed back into the checkdown-and-sack pattern of the last three weeks.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is structural. A team that passes this much keeps him in the 240-270 yard range against most opponents, and his downfield accuracy has held long enough to trust more than a hot streak. What I expect to regress is the recent sack spike. His pressure-to-sack rate was a strength the last two years, and the line should get healthier. The touchdown count is the shakier piece: the red-zone touchdowns have outrun a sub-30% success rate there, so expect closer to one and a half a game than two.

The floor is still lower than his September suggests. The screen game is a real drain. Against fast, disciplined fronts he has been pushed into a short game where he gives back value. The rest of the season probably lands between the two versions: efficiency around league average, high attempts, and a sack rate above the league norm.
swingFactors: Damien Lewis and the interior line's health
How many top pass rushes remain on the schedule

confidence.note: Seven games split between a hot start and a slump, with the line in flux.
